question: If $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 4\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$, find the vector projection of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}$ and verify that it is parallel to $\vec{b}$.
explanation:
Vector projection of $\vec{a}$ on $\vec{b}$ is $\text{proj}_{\vec{b}}\vec{a} = \left(\frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|^2}\right)\vec{b}$.

$\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = (2)(1)+(-3)(4)+(1)(-2) = -12$.

$|\vec{b}|^2 = 1^2+4^2+(-2)^2 = 21$.

Scalar factor $= -\frac{12}{21} = -\frac{4}{7}$.

Thus projection $= -\frac{4}{7}(\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k}) = -\frac{4}{7}\hat{i}-\frac{16}{7}\hat{j}+\frac{8}{7}\hat{k}$.

This is a scalar multiple of $\vec{b}$, hence it is parallel to $\vec{b}$.
